title.zh: 卷11 廢出三帝紀 前廢帝廣陵王
title.en: Volume 11 Annals: Three Emperors that Fled - Emperor Qianfei, Prince of Guangling (also Emperor Houfei and Emperor Xiaowu)
title.raw: 卷11 廢出三帝紀 前廢帝廣陵王 Volume 11 Annals: Three Emperors that Fled - Emperor Qianfei, Prince of Guangling (also Emperor Houfei and Emperor Xiaowu)

sentences.zh: 前廢帝廣陵王 後廢帝安定王 出帝平陽王

translations.literal: Deposed Emperor Qianfei, Prince of Guangling; Deposed Emperor Houfei, Prince of Anding; Emperor Chu, Prince of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Deposed Emperor Qianfei, Prince of Guangling; Deposed Emperor Houfei, Prince of Anding; Emperor Chu, Prince of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝，諱恭，字脩業，廣陵惠王羽之子也，母曰王氏。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor Qianfei bore the taboo name Gong, styled Xiuye; he was the son of Prince of Guangling Hui, Yu; his mother was Lady Wang.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor Qianfei bore the taboo name Gong, styled Xiuye. He was the son of Prince of Guangling Hui, Yu; his mother was Lady Wang.

sentences.zh: 少端謹，有志度。

translations.literal: In youth he was upright and careful, with purpose and measure.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was upright and careful, with steadiness of purpose.

sentences.zh: 長而好學，事祖母、嫡母以孝聞。

translations.literal: When grown he loved learning, and was famed for filial service to his grandmother and principal mother.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he loved learning and was famed for filial devotion to his grandmother and principal mother.

sentences.zh: 正始中，襲爵。

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi era he inherited the princely fief.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengshi era he inherited the princely title.

sentences.zh: 延昌中，拜通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the Yanchang era he was appointed direct-palace scattered cavalier attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yanchang era he was made direct-palace scattered cavalier attendant.

sentences.zh: 神龜中，進兼散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the Shengui era he was advanced to concurrent scattered cavalier attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shengui era he was advanced to concurrent scattered cavalier attendant.

sentences.zh: 正光二年，正常侍，領給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengguang he was regular attendant and concurrently chief of the yellow-gate secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengguang he became regular attendant and concurrently chief of the yellow-gate secretariat.

sentences.zh: 帝以元叉擅權，遂稱疾不起。

translations.literal: Because the emperor saw Yuan Cha monopolizing power, he then pleaded illness and would not attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Yuan Cha monopolize power, the prince pleaded illness and stopped attending court.

sentences.zh: 久之，因託瘖病。

translations.literal: After a long while he took refuge in muteness.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he feigned muteness.

sentences.zh: 五年，就除金紫光祿大夫，[1]加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed in situ grand master of splendid carriages with golden seal and purple cord, [1] with the additional title of scattered cavalier attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was given the post of grand master of splendid carriages with golden seal and purple cord, [1] and the additional title of scattered cavalier attendant.

sentences.zh: 建義元年，除儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyi he was made equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianyi he was made equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 王既絕言，垂將一紀，居於龍花寺，無所交通。

translations.literal: The prince had ceased speech and was approaching a full twelve-year cycle; he dwelt at Longhua Temple and had no dealings with others.
translations.idiomatic: The prince had not spoken for nearly twelve years. He lived at Longhua Temple and kept no company outside it.

sentences.zh: 永安末，有白莊帝者，言王不語將有異圖；

translations.literal: At the end of Yongan someone informed Emperor Xiaozhuang that the prince’s silence betokened a different design;
translations.idiomatic: Late in Yongan someone told Emperor Xiaozhuang that the prince’s silence hid treasonous intent;

sentences.zh: 民間遊聲，又云有天子之氣。

translations.literal: among the people wandering talk also said there was the aura of a Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: and street rumor claimed the aura of a true emperor clung to him.

sentences.zh: 王懼禍，逃匿上洛，尋見追躡，執送京師，拘禁多日，以無狀獲免。

translations.literal: The prince, fearing disaster, fled and hid at Shangluo; soon he was pursued and seized, sent to the capital, imprisoned many days, and released for lack of evidence.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing ruin, the prince fled to Shangluo; pursuers soon caught him and brought him to the capital. After many days in custody he was released—for nothing could be proved.

sentences.zh: 及莊帝崩，尒朱世隆等以元曄疏遠，又非人望所推，以王潛默晦身，有過人之量，將謀廢立，恐實不語，乃令王所親申其意，且兼迫脅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang died, Erzhu Shilong and others, because Yuan Ye was remote in kinship and not what men’s hopes pushed forward, saw in the prince’s hidden silence and retiring body a measure beyond others; they plotted to depose and install, feared he truly would not speak, and so had those close to the prince convey their intent, and also pressed him by force.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang died, Erzhu Shilong and his faction found Yuan Ye too remote in blood and too little esteemed to hold the throne. The prince’s long silence and retiring life seemed to hide uncommon depth; they resolved on a change of ruler. Fearing he would never break silence, they sent intimates to explain their wish—and backed the message with threats.

sentences.zh: 王遂答曰：「天何言哉！

translations.literal: The prince then answered: "Does Heaven speak?"
translations.idiomatic: The prince answered at last: "Does Heaven speak?"

sentences.zh: 」世隆等大悅。

translations.literal: Shilong and the rest were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong and the others were overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 春二月己巳，曄進至邙南，世隆等奉王東郭之外，行禪讓之禮，羣臣上表曰：「否泰沿時，殷憂啟聖，故六飛在御，三石興符。

translations.literal: Spring, second month, day jisi: Ye advanced to the south of Mang; Shilong and the rest received the prince outside the eastern suburb and performed the rite of abdication; the hundred officials submitted a memorial saying: "Decline and peace follow the times; deep sorrow opens the sage—thus the six dragons are in the saddle and the three stones rise as tokens."
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the second month, on jisi day, Yuan Ye advanced to the south of Mang. Shilong and his party received the prince outside the eastern suburb and performed the abdication rite. The hundred officials memorialized: "Fortune and misfortune turn with the age; grave peril summons the sage—thus the six dragons take the reins and the three stones bear heaven’s mandate."

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下運屬千齡，智周萬物，獨昭繫象，妙極天人，寶曆有歸，光宅攸屬，而將安獨善，不務兼濟，靈命徘徊，幽明載佇。

translations.literal: We bow and consider that Your Majesty’s fortune belongs to a thousand ages, wisdom encompasses the ten thousand things, alone you illumine the attached images, subtly you reach heaven and man; the precious succession has its place, glorious dwelling is yours—yet you would rest in solitary good and not pursue universal aid; the numinous mandate lingers, dark and bright alike wait.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly consider that Your Majesty’s fate spans a thousand ages and your wisdom embraces all things beneath heaven; you alone illumine the patterns of the Changes and penetrate the border of heaven and humanity. The sacred succession is yours, the bright dwelling rightly yours—yet you would keep to private good and refuse the common weal; the numinous charge still hesitates, and both realms of the living and the dead stand waiting.

sentences.zh: 伏願時順謳謠，念茲宗祏，用捨勞疾，允答人神。

translations.literal: We pray that you timely follow the songs of the people, think on this ancestral temple, lay aside weariness and illness, and truly answer man and spirit.
translations.idiomatic: We beg you to heed the people’s song, remember the ancestral shrine, put aside fatigue and sickness, and answer both men and spirits as heaven demands.

sentences.zh: 」王答曰：「自量眇身，是以讓執。

translations.literal: The prince answered: "Measuring my slight person, I therefore yielded the charge."
translations.idiomatic: The prince replied: "Knowing how slight I am, I yielded the throne."

sentences.zh: 然王公勤至，不可拒違。

translations.literal: Yet the kings and dukes were earnest to the utmost; one could not refuse and disobey.
translations.idiomatic: But the princes and ministers pressed with such zeal that refusal was impossible.

sentences.zh: 今敬承所陳，惟愧弗堪負荷耳。

translations.literal: Now I respectfully accept what you have set forth—only ashamed that I cannot bear the burden."
translations.idiomatic: I accept in reverence what you urge—ashamed only that I am unfit to bear so great a weight."

sentences.zh: 」太尉公尒朱度律奉進璽綬袞冕之服，乃就輅車，百官侍衞，入自建春、雲龍門，昇太極前殿，羣臣拜賀。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Erzhu Dulu presented the imperial seal and cord and robes of investiture; he then mounted the carriage; the hundred officials attended in guard; he entered by the Jianchun and Yunlong gates, ascended the Hall of Supreme Ultimate in the front palace, and the hundred officials bowed in congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Erzhu Dulu presented seal, cord, and robes of state. The prince mounted the imperial carriage; officials formed his escort. He entered through the Jianchun and Yunlong gates, ascended the front hall of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, and the court bowed in congratulation.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，登閶闔門，詔曰：「朕以寡薄，撫臨萬邦，思與億兆同茲慶泰。

translations.literal: When the rites were done he ascended the Changhe Gate and issued an edict: "We, with meager virtue, hold the myriad realms in care; we think to share this blessed peace with the hundred millions."
translations.idiomatic: The rites finished, he mounted the Changhe Gate and proclaimed: "We, of little merit, now rule the myriad lands; we mean to share this blessed peace with all the people."

sentences.zh: 可大赦天下，以魏為大魏，改建明二年為普泰元年。

translations.literal: A general amnesty may be declared throughout the realm; Wei is made Great Wei; the second year of Jianming is changed to the first year of Putai.
translations.idiomatic: Let there be a general amnesty; Wei shall be Great Wei; the second year of Jianming becomes the first year of Putai.

sentences.zh: 其稅市及稅鹽之官，可悉廢之。

translations.literal: Offices taxing markets and taxing salt may all be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: All offices that taxed markets and salt are abolished.

sentences.zh: 百雜之戶，貸賜民名，官任仍舊。

translations.literal: Households of miscellaneous trades were lent commoner status for names; official posts remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous-trade households were granted commoner standing in name; their official assignments stayed unchanged.

sentences.zh: 天下調絹，四百一匹。

translations.literal: The realm’s levy in silk: four hundred bolts per household.
translations.idiomatic: The empire’s silk levy was set at four hundred bolts per household.

sentences.zh: 內外文武，普汎四階；

translations.literal: Civil and military within and without: a universal promotion of four ranks;
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officers at court and in the provinces alike received a universal promotion of four ranks;

sentences.zh: 合敍未定第者，亦沾級。

translations.literal: those in combined seniority whose rank was not yet fixed also received rank.
translations.idiomatic: and those awaiting formal rank in combined seniority were also given a step.

sentences.zh: 除名免官者，特復本資，品封依舊。

translations.literal: Those struck from the rolls and dismissed from office were specially restored to original salary; noble rank and fief remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Men struck from the rolls or dismissed from office were restored to their former salaries; titles and fiefs stood unchanged.

sentences.zh: 潁川王尒朱兆，彭城王尒朱仲遠，隴西王尒朱天光，樂平王尒朱世隆，常山王尒朱度律，車騎大將軍、儀同三司齊獻武王，都督斛斯椿下軍士，普汎六級。

translations.literal: Prince of Yingchuan Erzhu Zhao, Prince of Pengcheng Erzhu Zhongyuan, Prince of Longxi Erzhu Tianguang, Prince of Leping Erzhu Shilong, Prince of Changshan Erzhu Dulu, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies Prince of Qi, Duke Xianwu Huan, and the officers and soldiers under Commander Husi Chun—all received a universal promotion of six ranks."
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yingchuan Erzhu Zhao, Prince of Pengcheng Erzhu Zhongyuan, Prince of Longxi Erzhu Tianguang, Prince of Leping Erzhu Shilong, Prince of Changshan Erzhu Dulu, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan, and the troops under Commander Husi Chun were all raised six ranks."

sentences.zh: 」庚午，詔曰：「朕以眇身，臨王公之上，夕惕祇懷，若履冰谷。

translations.literal: day gengwu: an edict said: "We, with slight person, preside above kings and dukes; evening and dawn we are reverently anxious, as if treading on ice in a ravine."
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day an edict said: "We, a slight man, sit above kings and dukes; from dusk to dawn we live in reverent fear, as though walking a gorge of ice."

sentences.zh: 賴七廟之靈，百辟忠誠之舉，庶免墜歿。

translations.literal: Relying on the spirits of the seven temples and the loyal exertions of the hundred ministers, we may perhaps escape ruin.
translations.idiomatic: By the seven temples’ spirits and the hundred ministers’ loyalty we may yet escape ruin.

sentences.zh: 夫三皇稱皇，五帝云帝，三代稱王，迭沖挹也。

translations.literal: The Three Sovereigns were called "emperor" in one way, the Five Thearchs "thearch," the Three Dynasties "king"—each in turn modestly yielded.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Sovereigns were called huang, the Five Thearchs di, the Three Dynasties wang—each age modestly held back the grander title.

sentences.zh: 自秦之末，競為皇帝。

translations.literal: From the end of Qin onward all vied to be huangdi—emperor.
translations.idiomatic: From Qin’s fall onward all contended for the title of emperor.

sentences.zh: 忘負乘之深殃，垂貪鄙於萬葉。

translations.literal: They forgot the deep calamity of bearing what their virtue could not sustain and bequeathed greedy baseness to ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: They forgot the catastrophe of a burden their virtue could not bear and passed greedy folly down through ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 予今稱帝，已為褒矣！

translations.literal: That we now call ourselves emperor is already praise enough!
translations.idiomatic: That we even call ourselves emperor is already more honor than we deserve!

sentences.zh: 可普告令知。」

translations.literal: Let this be proclaimed everywhere so all may know."
translations.idiomatic: Let this be proclaimed throughout the realm."

sentences.zh: 是月，鎮遠將軍清河崔祖螭聚青州七郡之眾十餘萬人圍東陽。

translations.literal: That month Pacifying-the-Distance General Cui Zuchi of Qinghe gathered more than a hundred thousand men from seven commanderies of Qing Province and besieged Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: That month Cui Zuchi of Qinghe, pacifying-the-distance general, raised more than a hundred thousand men from seven Qing commanderies and besieged Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 幽州刺史劉靈助起兵於薊。

translations.literal: Regional Inspector of You Province Liu Lingzhu raised troops at Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lingzhu, regional inspector of You, raised troops at Ji.

sentences.zh: 撫軍將軍、金紫光祿大夫、兼侍中、河北大使高乾邕及弟平北將軍、通直散騎常侍敖曹，率眾夜襲冀州，執刺史元嶷，殺監軍孫白鷂，共推前河內太守封隆之行州事。

translations.literal: Pacification-General Gao Gan’ou, grand master of splendid carriages with golden seal and purple cord and concurrent attendant, Hebei grand envoy, and his younger brother Pacifier of the North, direct-palace scattered cavalier attendant Aocao, led troops by night to surprise Ji Province, seized Regional Inspector Yuan Yi, killed Supervising General Sun Baiyao, and together set up former Administrator of Henei Feng Longzhi to handle provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gan’ou, pacification-general, grand master of splendid carriages with golden seal and purple cord, concurrent attendant, and Hebei grand envoy, with his younger brother Aocao, pacifier of the north and direct-palace scattered cavalier attendant, led a night raid on Ji Province, seized Yuan Yi the inspector, killed supervising general Sun Baiyao, and installed former Henei administrator Feng Longzhi to govern the province.

sentences.zh: 三月癸酉，封長廣王曄為東海王。

translations.literal: Third month, day guiyou: Prince of Changgung Ye was enfeoffed Prince of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou day in the third month Prince of Changgung Ye was made prince of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 詔太師、驃騎大將軍、青州刺史、魯郡王肅還為太師；

translations.literal: An edict made Grand Preceptor, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Regional Inspector of Qing Province, and Prince of Lu Commandery Su return to the post of grand preceptor;
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored Grand Preceptor Su, grand general of agile cavalry, regional inspector of Qing, and prince of Lu commandery, to grand preceptor;

sentences.zh: 特進、車騎大將軍、沛郡王欣為太傅、司州牧，改封淮陽王；

translations.literal: Special Advance, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Prince of Pei Commandery Xin was made Grand Tutor and Governor of Si Province, and his fief was changed to Prince of Huaiyang;
translations.idiomatic: Xin, special advance, grand general of chariots and cavalry, and prince of Pei, was made grand tutor and governor of Si, with his fief changed to Huaiyang;

sentences.zh: 驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、徐州刺史、彭城王尒朱仲遠，驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、雍州刺史、隴西王尒朱天光，並為大將軍；

translations.literal: Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Commissioner with Full Powers Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, Regional Inspector of Xu Province, Prince of Pengcheng Erzhu Zhongyuan, and Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, Regional Inspector of Yong Province, Prince of Longxi Erzhu Tianguang—both were made grand generals;
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhongyuan, prince of Pengcheng, grand general of agile cavalry, commissioner with full powers equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, and inspector of Xu, and Erzhu Tianguang, prince of Longxi, grand general of agile cavalry, equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, and inspector of Yong, were both made grand generals;

sentences.zh: 柱國大將軍、并州刺史、潁川王尒朱兆為天柱大將軍；

translations.literal: Pillar Grand General, Regional Inspector of Bing Province, Prince of Yingchuan Erzhu Zhao was made Pillar of Heaven Grand General;
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao, pillar grand general, regional inspector of Bing, and prince of Yingchuan, was made pillar of heaven grand general;

sentences.zh: 驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、左衞將軍、大都督、晉州刺史、平陽郡開國公齊獻武王封勃海王，增邑五百戶；

translations.literal: Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, General of the Left Guard, Grand Commander, Regional Inspector of Jin Province, and Duke of Pingyang Commandery with an open state, Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan, was enfeoffed Prince of Bohai, fief increased by five hundred households;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan, grand general of agile cavalry, equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, general of the left guard, grand commander, regional inspector of Jin, and state-founding duke of Pingyang commandery, was enfeoffed prince of Bohai with five hundred added households;

sentences.zh: 特進、車騎大將軍、清河王亶為儀同三司；

translations.literal: Special Advance, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Prince of Qinghe Dan was made Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies;
translations.idiomatic: Dan, prince of Qinghe, special advance and grand general of chariots and cavalry, was made equal in honor to the Three Excellencies;

sentences.zh: 侍中、太傅、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、尚書令、樂平王尒朱世隆為太保；

translations.literal: Attendant, Grand Tutor, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Commissioner with Full Powers Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Leping Erzhu Shilong was made Grand Guardian;
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Shilong, prince of Leping, attendant, grand tutor, grand general of agile cavalry, commissioner with full powers equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, and director of the Masters of Writing, was made grand guardian;

sentences.zh: 開府、前司徒公長孫稚為太尉公、錄尚書事；

translations.literal: Commissioner with Full Powers, former Minister over the Masses Changsun Zhi was made Grand Preceptor and recorder of Secretariat affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Zhi, commissioner with full powers and former minister over the masses, was made grand preceptor and recorder of secretariat affairs;

sentences.zh: 侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、趙郡王諶為司空公。

translations.literal: Attendant, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Commissioner with Full Powers Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, Prince of Zhao Commandery Chen was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Chen, prince of Zhao commandery, attendant, grand general of agile cavalry, and commissioner with full powers equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, was made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 稚固辭，尋除驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Zhi firmly declined; soon he was made Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Commissioner with Full Powers Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi declined firmly; soon he was made grand general of agile cavalry and commissioner with full powers equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 丙子，帝引見尚書右僕射元羅及皇宗於顯陽殿，勞勉之。

translations.literal: day bingzi: the emperor received in audience Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Luo and the imperial clan at the Xianyang Hall and comforted and exhorted them.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day the emperor received Yuan Luo, right vice director of the Masters of Writing, and the imperial clan at Xianyang Hall and exhorted them with words of comfort.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，加驃騎大將軍、北華州刺史公孫略儀同三司。

translations.literal: day dingchou: Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Regional Inspector of North Hua Gongsun Lue was given the additional title Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day Gongsun Lue, grand general of agile cavalry and regional inspector of North Hua, was given the additional title equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 己卯，詔右衞將軍賀拔勝并尚書一人募伎作及雜戶從征者，正入出身，皆授實官，私馬者優一大階。

translations.literal: day jimao: an edict ordered General of the Right Guard Heba Sheng together with one person from the Masters of Writing to recruit performers and miscellaneous households for the campaign; on formal entry to service all were given substantive office; those with private horses received one major preferential rank.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day an edict ordered Heba Sheng, general of the right guard, with one Master of Writing to recruit performers and miscellaneous households for the campaign; on entering service all received substantive posts; men who brought private horses gained one major preferential step.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，以侍中、衞將軍、咸陽王坦，衞將軍、尚書左僕射、南陽王寶炬，侍中、征東將軍、平陽王脩，並儀同三司。

translations.literal: day gengchen: Attendant, General of the Guard, Prince of Xianyang Tan; General of the Guard, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Nanyang Baoju; Attendant, Pacification-General of the East, Prince of Pingyang Xiu—all were made Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen day Tan, prince of Xianyang, attendant and general of the guard; Baoju, prince of Nanyang, general of the guard and left vice director of the Masters of Writing; and Xiu, prince of Pingyang, attendant and pacification-general of the east, were all made equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，詔簡北來及在京二官員外剩置者。

translations.literal: day yiyou: an edict ordered selection among northerners who had come and among surplus supernumerary officials of the two ministries in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou day an edict ordered a purge of supernumerary officials among recent arrivals from the north and surplus staff in the two capital ministries.

sentences.zh: 己丑，以持節、驃騎將軍、涇州刺史賀拔岳為儀同三司、岐州刺史，使持節、車騎大將軍、渭州刺史侯莫陳悅為儀同三司、秦州刺史。

translations.literal: day jichou: Bearer of the Staff, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Regional Inspector of Jing Province Heba Yue was made Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies and Regional Inspector of Qi; Bearer of the Staff, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Regional Inspector of Wei Province Houmochen Yue was made Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies and Regional Inspector of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou day Heba Yue, bearer of the staff, grand general of agile cavalry, and inspector of Jing, was made equal in honor to the Three Excellencies and inspector of Qi; Houmochen Yue, bearer of the staff, grand general of chariots and cavalry, and inspector of Wei, was made equal in honor to the Three Excellencies and inspector of Qin.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，詔天下有德孝仁賢忠義志信者，可以禮召赴闕，不應召者以不敬論。

translations.literal: day gengyin: an edict said that throughout the realm men of virtue, filial piety, benevolence, worth, loyalty, righteousness, resolve, and trust might be summoned to court by ritual invitation; those who did not answer the summons were to be judged disrespectful.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin day an edict invited men of virtue, filial piety, benevolence, worth, loyalty, righteousness, resolve, and trust throughout the realm to court by ceremonial summons; refusal was to be punished as disrespect.

sentences.zh: 丙申，劉靈助率眾次於安國城，定州刺史侯淵破斬之，傳首京師。

translations.literal: day bingshen: Liu Lingzhu led his host to camp at Anguo city; Regional Inspector of Ding Province Hou Yuan defeated and beheaded him and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen day Liu Lingzhu encamped at Anguo; Hou Yuan, regional inspector of Ding, routed and killed him and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，以使持節、侍中、車騎大將軍斛斯椿，侍中、衞將軍元受，並特進、儀同三司。

translations.literal: day wuxu: Bearer of the Staff, Attendant, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry Husi Chun, and Attendant, General of the Guard Yuan Shou—both were made Special Advance and Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu day Husi Chun, bearer of the staff, attendant, and grand general of chariots and cavalry, and Yuan Shou, attendant and general of the guard, were both made special advance and equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「頃官方失序，仍令沙汰，定員簡剩，已有判決。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Recently official posts fell out of order and we still ordered a purge; fixed quotas were trimmed and surplus judged—decisions are already rendered."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Official posts have lately fallen into disorder and we ordered a purge; quotas were fixed and surplus cut—judgments are already rendered."

sentences.zh: 退下之徒，微亦可愍。

translations.literal: Those cast down may in small measure also be pitied.
translations.idiomatic: Those who fell in the purge deserve some pity as well.

sentences.zh: 諸在簡下，可特優一級，皆授將軍，預參選限，隨能補用。」

translations.literal: All who were on the purge list may specially receive one preferential rank, all be made generals, enter the selection quota, and be placed according to ability."
translations.idiomatic: All on the purge list shall receive one preferential rank, be made generals, enter the selection rolls, and be placed as their talents allow."

sentences.zh: 是春，冠軍將軍、南青州刺史茹懷朗使其部將何寶率步騎三千擊蕭衍守將於琅邪，擒其尚書左僕射、儀同三司、雲麾將軍、徐兗二州刺史劉相如。

translations.literal: That spring Champion General and Regional Inspector of South Qing Ru Huailang had his subordinate commander He Bao lead three thousand foot and horse to attack Xiao Yan’s garrison commander at Langye and captured Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, Cloud-Banner General, and Regional Inspector of Xu and Yan Provinces Liu Xiangru.
translations.idiomatic: That spring Ru Huailang, champion general and regional inspector of South Qing, sent his commander He Bao with three thousand foot and horse against Xiao Yan’s garrison at Langye and took Liu Xiangru—left vice director of the Masters of Writing, equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, cloud-banner general, and joint inspector of Xu and Yan.

translations.literal: The text is deficient.
translations.idiomatic: The text is deficient.

sentences.zh: 夏四月癸卯，幸華林都亭燕射，班錫有差。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day guimao: the emperor visited the Capital Pavilion in the Hualin Park for archery feast; gifts were distributed in differing measure.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao day in the fourth month of summer the emperor feasted with archery at the Capital Pavilion in Hualin Park; gifts were graded by rank.

sentences.zh: 太樂奏伎有倡優為愚癡者，帝以非雅戲，詔罷之。

translations.literal: The Grand Music Office performed; among the entertainers were buffoons playing idiots; the emperor, because it was not refined amusement, ordered it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Music Office performed; some buffoons played the fool. The emperor, finding the show unworthy of court, ordered it stopped.

sentences.zh: 壬子，有事於太廟。

translations.literal: day renzi: there was service at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi day the court sacrificed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，詔以齊獻武王為使持節、侍中、都督冀州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、大都督、東道大行臺、冀州刺史，驃騎大將軍、安定王尒朱智虎為開府儀同三司、肆州刺史。

translations.literal: day guichou: an edict made Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan bearer of the staff, attendant, commander of all military affairs of Ji Province, grand general of agile cavalry, commissioner with full powers equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, grand commander, eastern-route grand mobile office, and regional inspector of Ji; Grand General of Agile Cavalry Prince of Anding Erzhu Zhihu was made commissioner with full powers equal in honor to the Three Excellencies and regional inspector of Si.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou day an edict made Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan bearer of the staff, attendant, commander of Ji military affairs, grand general of agile cavalry, commissioner with full powers equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, grand commander, eastern-route grand mobile office, and inspector of Ji; Erzhu Zhihu, prince of Anding, grand general of agile cavalry, was made commissioner with full powers equal in honor to the Three Excellencies and inspector of Si.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，以右衞將軍賀拔勝、武衞將軍大野拔並為儀同三司。

translations.literal: day yimao: General of the Right Guard Heba Sheng and General of the Martial Guard Daye Ba were both made Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day Heba Sheng, general of the right guard, and Daye Ba, general of the martial guard, were both made equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 己未，帝於顯陽殿簡試通直散騎常侍、散騎侍郎、通直郎，剩員非才他轉之。

translations.literal: day jiwei: at the Xianyang Hall the emperor conducted a selection test of direct-palace scattered cavalier attendants, scattered cavalier attendants, and direct-palace gentlemen; surplus posts held by men without talent were transferred elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei day at Xianyang Hall the emperor tested direct-palace scattered cavalier attendants, scattered cavalier attendants, and direct-palace gentlemen; surplus posts held by unfit men were reassigned.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，隴西王尒朱天光大破宿勤明達，擒送京師，斬之。

translations.literal: day guihai: Prince of Longxi Erzhu Tianguang greatly defeated Suqin Mingda, captured him and sent him to the capital, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day Erzhu Tianguang, prince of Longxi, routed Suqin Mingda, sent him captive to the capital, and had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，以侍中、驃騎大將軍尒朱彥伯為司徒公。

translations.literal: day bingyin: Attendant and Grand General of Agile Cavalry Erzhu Yanbo was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day Erzhu Yanbo, attendant and grand general of agile cavalry, was made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 詔有司不得復稱偽梁，罷細作之條，無禁鄰國往還。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices not again to call Liang by the name "false"; the statute on fine manufacture was abolished; no ban was placed on traffic with neighboring states.
translations.idiomatic: An edict forbade officials to call the Liang "false" any longer, abolished the fine-manufacture statute, and lifted bans on trade with neighboring states.

sentences.zh: 詔員外諫議大夫、步兵校尉、奉車都尉、羽林監、給事中、積射將軍、奉朝請、殿中將軍、宮門僕射、殿中司馬督、治禮郎十一官，得俸而不給力，老合外選者，依常格，其未老欲外選者，聽解。

translations.literal: An edict [listed] eleven posts—supplementary adviser, infantry commandant, director of imperial carriages, supervisor of the feathered guard, gentleman within the yellow gate, standing-shoot general, court gentleman, palace general, gate gentleman of the palace, supervisor of palace attendants, director of palace attendants, master of rites—who received salary but gave no labor service: those old enough for outside selection followed the regular rule; those not yet old who wished outside selection were permitted to resign.
translations.idiomatic: An edict named eleven posts—from supplementary adviser through master of rites—that drew salary without labor duty: men old enough for outside appointment kept the usual rule; younger men who wished to leave for outside posts might resign.

sentences.zh: 其七品以上，朔望入朝，若正員有闕，隨才進補。

translations.literal: From the seventh rank upward they entered court on the first and fifteenth of the month; if a regular post was vacant, men were advanced according to talent.
translations.idiomatic: From the seventh rank up, officers attended court on the first and fifteenth; when a regular post fell vacant, talent filled it.

sentences.zh: 前員外簡退優階者追之，稱事簡下者，仍優一級。

translations.literal: Former supernumeraries who had been purged and given preferential rank had it revoked; those called surplus by circumstance still received one preferential rank.
translations.idiomatic: Former supernumeraries who had gained preferential rank in the purge had it taken back; men still listed as surplus received one preferential step.

sentences.zh: 先是，南陽太守趙脩延執刺史李琰之；

translations.literal: Earlier, Administrator of Nanyang Zhao Xiuyan had seized Regional Inspector Li Yanzhi;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhao Xiuyan, administrator of Nanyang, had seized Li Yanzhi the regional inspector;

sentences.zh: 五月丙子，荊州城民斬脩延，送首，還推琰之為刺史。

translations.literal: fifth month, day bingzi: the people of Jing Province city beheaded Xiuyan, sent his head, and in turn set up Yanzhi as regional inspector.
translations.idiomatic: on bingzi day in the fifth month the people of Jing provincial city killed Xiuyan, sent his head, and restored Yanzhi as inspector.

sentences.zh: 尒朱仲遠使其都督魏僧勗等討崔祖螭於東陽，擒斬之。

translations.literal: Erzhu Zhongyuan sent his commander Wei Sengqin and others to attack Cui Zuchi at Dongyang; they captured and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhongyuan sent Wei Sengqin and other commanders against Cui Zuchi at Dongyang and killed him.

sentences.zh: 六月庚申，齊獻武王以尒朱逆亂，始興義兵於信都。

translations.literal: sixth month, day gengshen: Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan, because the Erzhu faction were rebels, first raised the banner of righteous troops at Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day in the sixth month Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan, judging the Erzhu clan rebels, first raised righteous troops at Xindu.

sentences.zh: 西定殷州，斬其刺史尒朱羽生，命南趙郡太守李元忠為刺史，鎮廣阿。

translations.literal: He pacified Yin Province in the west, beheaded its regional inspector Erzhu Yusheng, appointed Administrator of South Zhao Commandery Li Yuanzhong regional inspector, and garrisoned Guang’a.
translations.idiomatic: He secured Yin in the west, beheaded Erzhu Yusheng the inspector, made Li Yuanzhong, administrator of South Zhao, inspector, and garrisoned Guang’a.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，帝臨顯陽殿，親理冤訟。

translations.literal: day guihai: the emperor came to the Xianyang Hall and personally judged wrongful suits.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day the emperor sat at Xianyang Hall and heard wrongful suits in person.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，以使持節、驃騎大將軍、開府尒朱弼為儀同三司。

translations.literal: day wuchen: Bearer of the Staff, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Commissioner with Full Powers Erzhu Bi was made Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen day Erzhu Bi, bearer of the staff, grand general of agile cavalry, and commissioner with full powers, was made equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 秋七月壬申，尒朱世隆等害前太保楊椿、前司空公楊津及其家。

translations.literal: seventh month of autumn, day renshen: Erzhu Shilong and others killed former Grand Guardian Yang Chun, former Minister of Works Yang Jin, and their families.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day in the seventh month of autumn Erzhu Shilong and his party murdered former grand guardian Yang Chun, former minister of works Yang Jin, and their kin.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，司徒公尒朱彥伯以旱遜位。

translations.literal: day bingxu: Minister of Works Erzhu Yanbo resigned his post because of drought.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu day Erzhu Yanbo, minister of works, resigned citing drought.

sentences.zh: 戊子，除彥伯侍中、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: day wuzi: Yanbo was made attendant and commissioner with full powers equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi day Yanbo was made attendant and commissioner with full powers equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，以侍中、太保、開府、尚書令、樂平王尒朱世隆為儀同三師，[3]位次上公。

translations.literal: day gengyin: Attendant, Grand Guardian, Commissioner with Full Powers, Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Leping Erzhu Shilong was made Equal in Honor to the Three Preceptors, [3] ranking below the supreme dukes.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin day Erzhu Shilong, prince of Leping, attendant, grand guardian, commissioner with full powers, and director of the Masters of Writing, was made equal in honor to the three preceptors, [3] ranking just below the supreme dukes.

sentences.zh: 八月庚子，詔隴西王尒朱天光下文武討宿勤明達者，汎三級。

translations.literal: eighth month, day gengzi: an edict ordered a universal promotion of three ranks for civil and military under Prince of Longxi Erzhu Tianguang who had gone down to attack Suqin Mingda.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day in the eighth month an edict raised three ranks for all civil and military who had followed Erzhu Tianguang, prince of Longxi, against Suqin Mingda.

sentences.zh: 潁川王尒朱兆率步騎二萬出井陘，趨殷州，李元忠棄城還信都。

translations.literal: Prince of Yingchuan Erzhu Zhao led twenty thousand foot and horse out by Jingxing, hastened toward Yin Province; Li Yuanzhong abandoned the city and returned to Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao, prince of Yingchuan, marched twenty thousand foot and horse through Jingxing toward Yin; Li Yuanzhong abandoned the city and fled back to Xindu.

sentences.zh: 丙午，常山王尒朱度律、彭城王尒朱仲遠等率眾出抗義旗。

translations.literal: day bingwu: Prince of Changshan Erzhu Dulu, Prince of Pengcheng Erzhu Zhongyuan, and others led hosts out to resist the banner of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu day Erzhu Dulu, prince of Changshan, Erzhu Zhongyuan, prince of Pengcheng, and others marched out to crush the righteous army.

sentences.zh: 九月丁丑，以侍中驃騎將軍盧同、驃騎大將軍杜德、車騎大將軍橋寧並為儀同三司。

translations.literal: ninth month, day dingchou: Attendant and Grand General of Agile Cavalry Lu Tong, Grand General of Agile Cavalry Du De, and Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry Qiao Ning were all made Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day in the ninth month Lu Tong, attendant and grand general of agile cavalry; Du De, grand general of agile cavalry; and Qiao Ning, grand general of chariots and cavalry, were all made equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 己卯，以使持節、都督東道諸軍事、兼尚書令、東道大行臺、彭城王尒朱仲遠為太宰。

translations.literal: day jimao: Bearer of the Staff, Commander of all Military Affairs of the Eastern Route, Concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing, Eastern-Route Grand Mobile Office, Prince of Pengcheng Erzhu Zhongyuan was made Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day Erzhu Zhongyuan, prince of Pengcheng, bearer of the staff, commander of eastern-route armies, concurrent director of the Masters of Writing, and eastern-route grand mobile office, was made grand mentor.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，加使持節、大將軍、都督關中諸軍事、兼尚書令、西道大行臺、隴西王尒朱天光為大司馬。

translations.literal: day gengchen: Bearer of the Staff, Grand General, Commander of all Military Affairs of Guanzhong, Concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing, Western-Route Grand Mobile Office, Prince of Longxi Erzhu Tianguang was advanced to Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen day Erzhu Tianguang, prince of Longxi, bearer of the staff, grand general, commander of Guanzhong armies, concurrent director of the Masters of Writing, and western-route grand mobile office, was advanced to grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 驃騎大將軍、青州刺史、開府儀同三司穆紹薨。

translations.literal: Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Regional Inspector of Qing Province, Commissioner with Full Powers Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies Mu Shao died.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Shao, grand general of agile cavalry, regional inspector of Qing, and commissioner with full powers equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, died.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，追尊皇考為先帝，皇妣王氏為先太妃；

translations.literal: day guisi: the late emperor-father was posthumously honored as Former Emperor; the late empress-dowager Lady Wang as Former Grand Consort;
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day the late emperor, his father, was posthumously honored Former Emperor; Lady Wang, his mother, Former Grand Consort;

sentences.zh: 封皇弟永業為高密王，皇子子恕為勃海王。

translations.literal: the emperor’s younger brother Yongye was enfeoffed Prince of Gaomi; the imperial son Zishu was enfeoffed Prince of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor’s brother Yongye was made prince of Gaomi; the prince’s son Zishu, prince of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 冬十月壬寅，齊獻武王推勃海太守元朗即皇帝位於信都。

translations.literal: winter, tenth month, day renyin: Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan set up Yuan Lang, administrator of Bohai, as emperor at Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin day in the tenth month of winter Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan enthroned Yuan Lang, administrator of Bohai, at Xindu.

sentences.zh: 二年春三月，齊獻武王敗尒朱天光等於韓陵。

translations.literal: spring, third month of the second year: Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan defeated Erzhu Tianguang and others at Hanling.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of spring in the second year Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan routed Erzhu Tianguang and his allies at Hanling.

translations.literal: The text is deficient.
translations.idiomatic: The text is deficient.

sentences.zh: 夏四月辛巳，齊獻武王與廢帝至邙山，使魏蘭根慰諭洛邑，且觀帝之為人。

translations.literal: summer, fourth month, day xinsi: Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan and the Deposed Emperor came to Mount Mang; he sent Wei Langen to comfort and instruct Luoyang and also observe the emperor’s character.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day in the fourth month of summer Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan brought the Deposed Emperor to Mount Mang and sent Wei Langen to reassure Luoyang—and to take the measure of the man on the throne.

sentences.zh: 蘭根忌帝雅德，還致毀謗，竟從崔㥄議，廢帝於崇訓佛寺，而立平陽王脩為帝。

translations.literal: Langen resented the emperor’s refined virtue; on his return he slandered him; in the end they followed Cui Ling’s counsel, deposed the emperor at Chongxun Buddhist temple, and set up Prince of Pingyang Xiu as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Langen envied the emperor’s quiet dignity; back at camp he poisoned Huan’s ear against him. They took Cui Ling’s advice, deposed the ruler at Chongxun Temple, and enthroned Xiu, prince of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 帝既失位，乃賦詩曰：「朱門久可患，紫極非情玩。

translations.literal: The emperor, having lost the throne, then composed a poem: "Crimson gates long breed sorrow; the purple apex is no place for fond play."
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of the throne, he wrote a poem: "Crimson gates have long been worth dread; the purple summit is no toy for the heart."

sentences.zh: 顛覆立可待，一年三易換。

translations.literal: Overthrow and enthronement wait close at hand; thrice in one year the throne changes hands.
translations.idiomatic: Ruin and renewal stand ready; three times in a single year the throne has changed hands.

sentences.zh: 時運正如此，唯有修真觀。」

translations.literal: The age’s fortune is just like this—only cultivating truth in contemplation remains."
translations.idiomatic: Fortune runs exactly so—only to cultivate truth in stillness is left."

sentences.zh: 太昌初，帝殂於門下外省，時年三十五。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang the emperor died in the outer office of the Gate Department; he was thirty-five years old.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taichang the Deposed Emperor died in the outer quarters of the Gate Department, aged thirty-five.

sentences.zh: 出帝詔百司赴會，大鴻臚監護喪事，葬用王禮，加以九旒、鑾輅、黃屋、左纛，班劍百二十人，二衞、羽林備儀衞。

translations.literal: Emperor Chu ordered the hundred offices to attend the mourning; the Grand Herald supervised the funeral; burial followed princely rite, with the addition of nine tassels, imperial carriage bells, yellow canopy, left great-banner, a hundred twenty halberds in formation, and full guard from the two guards and feathered guard.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Chu ordered the ministries to the funeral; the grand herald oversaw the rites. He was buried with princely honors plus nine tassels, imperial bells, yellow canopy, left great-banner, a hundred twenty halberds in formation, and escort from both palace guards and the feathered guard.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝，諱朗，字仲哲，章武王融第三子也，母曰程氏。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor Houfei bore the taboo name Lang, styled Zhongzhe; he was the third son of Prince of Zhangwu Rong; his mother was Lady Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor Houfei bore the taboo name Lang, styled Zhongzhe. He was the third son of Prince of Zhangwu Rong; his mother was Lady Cheng.

sentences.zh: 少稱明悟。

translations.literal: In youth he was famed as bright and perceptive.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was praised for quick understanding.

sentences.zh: 永安二年，為肆州魯郡王後軍府錄事參軍、儀同開府司馬。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongan he was recorder of the rear army headquarters of Prince of Lu Commandery of Si Province and commissioner with full powers, open-office staff major.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongan he served as recorder of the rear-army headquarters of the prince of Lu in Si and as open-office staff major with commissioner’s powers.

sentences.zh: 元曄之建明二年正月戊子，為冀州勃海太守。

translations.literal: On day wuzi in the first month of the second year of Jianming under Yuan Ye he was made Administrator of Bohai in Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi day in the first month of Jianming year two under Yuan Ye he became administrator of Bohai in Ji.

sentences.zh: 及齊獻武王起義兵，將誅暴逆，乃推戴之。

translations.literal: When Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan raised the army of righteousness to punish violent rebels, he was set up and carried on the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan raised righteous troops to punish the tyrants, Lang was pushed onto the throne.

sentences.zh: 十有一月己巳，詔曰：「王度創開，彝倫方始，所班官秩，不改舊章。

translations.literal: eleventh month, day jisi: an edict said: "Royal measure is newly opened, ritual order just begun; official ranks issued remain under the old statutes."
translations.idiomatic: On jisi day in the eleventh month an edict said: "The royal measure is newly opened and ritual order only begun; the ranks we issue still follow the old statutes."

sentences.zh: 而無識之徒，因茲僥倖，謬增軍級，虛名顯位，皆言前朝所授，理難推抑。

translations.literal: Yet men without understanding seized this chance; they wrongly added military rank and empty names with lofty posts, all saying they were conferred by the former court—hard to push back on principle."
translations.idiomatic: Yet the witless seized the moment: they padded military rank and bought hollow titles, all claiming grants from the fallen court—titles hard to revoke in law.

sentences.zh: 自非嚴為條制，無以防其偽竊。

translations.literal: Unless strict regulations are made, there is no way to guard against false seizure."
translations.idiomatic: Without stern rules there is no stopping the fraud."

sentences.zh: 諸有虛增官號，為人發糾，罪從軍法。

translations.literal: All who falsely added official titles and are denounced by others—punishment follows military law."
translations.idiomatic: Whoever padded his title and is exposed shall be punished under military law."

sentences.zh: 若入格檢覈無名者，退為平民，終身禁錮。

translations.literal: If on inspection the name does not fit the register, he is demoted to commoner and imprisoned for life."
translations.idiomatic: If the rolls cannot verify the rank, he is reduced to commoner and imprisoned for life."

sentences.zh: 」庚辰，齊獻武王率師攻鄴城。

translations.literal: day gengchen: Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan led the army to attack Ye city.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen day Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan marched against Ye.

sentences.zh: 是年，南兗城民王乞德逼前刺史劉世明以州降蕭衍，衍使其將元樹入據譙城。

translations.literal: That year the people of Nan Yan city forced former Regional Inspector Liu Shiming to surrender the province to Xiao Yan; Yan sent his general Yuan Shu to enter and hold Qiao city.
translations.idiomatic: That year the people of Nan Yan compelled Liu Shiming, former inspector, to hand the province to Xiao Yan; Yan’s general Yuan Shu seized Qiao.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月壬午，拔鄴，擒刺史劉誕。

translations.literal: spring, first month, day renwu: Ye was taken; Regional Inspector Liu Dan was captured.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day in the first month of spring Ye fell; Liu Dan the inspector was taken.

sentences.zh: 詔諸將士汎四級，封侯、增邑九十七人，各有差等。

translations.literal: An edict ordered a universal promotion of four ranks for generals and soldiers; ninety-seven were enfeoffed marquis and given increased fiefs, each in differing measure.
translations.idiomatic: An edict raised every soldier four ranks; ninety-seven men were made marquises with added fiefs, each according to merit.

sentences.zh: 癸未，詔曰：「自中興草昧，典制權輿，郡縣之官，率多行、督。

translations.literal: day guiwei: an edict said: "Since the revival in hardship, institutions were improvised; commandery and district officials were mostly acting supervisors and overseers."
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei day an edict said: "Since our revival from chaos, law was makeshift; most commandery and district officers were only acting supervisors or overseers."

sentences.zh: 假有正者，風化未均。

translations.literal: Even where there were regular appointees, custom and teaching were not yet even.
translations.idiomatic: Even regular appointees could not yet spread even rule.

sentences.zh: 眷彼周餘，專為漁獵。

translations.literal: They looked on the remnant of Zhou as nothing but prey for the net.
translations.idiomatic: They treated what remained of Zhou’s order as mere quarry for the hunter.

sentences.zh: 朕所以夙興夜寐，有惕於懷。

translations.literal: We therefore rise early and sleep late, ever anxious in our breast.
translations.idiomatic: We rise before dawn and sleep after dark, uneasy in heart.

sentences.zh: 有司明加糾罰，稱朕意焉。」

translations.literal: Let the relevant offices clearly add correction and punishment—this matches our intent."
translations.idiomatic: Let the ministries punish without mercy—that is our will."

sentences.zh: 二月辛亥，上孝莊皇帝諡曰武懷皇帝。

translations.literal: second month, day xinhai: Emperor Xiaozhuang was given the posthumous title Emperor Wu the Cherishing.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai day in the second month Emperor Xiaozhuang received the posthumous title Emperor Wu the Cherishing.

sentences.zh: 甲子，以齊獻武王為大丞相、柱國大將軍、太師，增封三萬戶，并前為六萬戶。

translations.literal: day jiazi: Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan was made Grand Chancellor, Pillar Grand General, and Grand Preceptor; fief was increased by thirty thousand households, thirty thousand together with the former making sixty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan was made grand chancellor, pillar grand general, and grand preceptor; his fief grew by thirty thousand households to sixty thousand in all.

sentences.zh: 三月丙寅，以齊文襄王起家為驃騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: third month, day bingyin: Prince of Qi Wenxiang began his career as Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day in the third month Prince of Qi Wenxiang first took office as grand general of agile cavalry and equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 丙子，以侍中、車騎大將軍、尚書左僕射孫騰為驃騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: day bingzi: Attendant, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Sun Teng was made Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day Sun Teng, attendant, grand general of chariots and cavalry, and left vice director of the Masters of Writing, was made grand general of agile cavalry and equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，車駕幸鄴。

translations.literal: day dingchou: the imperial carriage visited Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day the court moved to Ye.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，詔文武家屬自信都赴鄴城。

translations.literal: day yiyou: an edict ordered civil and military families from Xindu to come to Ye city.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou day an edict summoned officials’ families from Xindu to Ye.

sentences.zh: 閏月乙未，以安北將軍、光祿大夫、博野縣開國伯尉景為驃騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: intercalary month, day yiwei: Pacifier of the North, Grand Master of Splendid Carriages, and State-Founding Earl of Boye Wei Jing was made Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei day in the intercalary month Wei Jing, pacifier of the north, grand master of splendid carriages, and state-founding earl of Boye, was made grand general of agile cavalry and equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 丙申，以衞將軍、金紫光祿大夫厙狄干為車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: day bingshen: General of the Guard, Grand Master of Splendid Carriages with Golden Seal and Purple Cord Kudi Gan was made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen day Kudi Gan, general of the guard and grand master of splendid carriages with golden seal and purple cord, was made grand general of chariots and cavalry and equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，尒朱天光、兆、度律、仲遠等屯於洹水之南。

translations.literal: day renyin: Erzhu Tianguang, Zhao, Dulu, Zhongyuan, and others encamped south of the Huan River.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin day Erzhu Tianguang, Zhao, Dulu, Zhongyuan, and the rest camped south of the Huan.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，齊獻武王出頓紫陌。

translations.literal: day guichou: Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan halted at Zimo.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou day Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan encamped at Zimo.

sentences.zh: 庚申，尒朱兆率輕騎三千夜襲鄴城，叩西門，不克，退走。

translations.literal: day gengshen: Erzhu Zhao led three thousand light horse in a night raid on Ye city, struck the west gate, failed to take it, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day Erzhu Zhao struck Ye by night with three thousand light horse, hammered the west gate, failed, and fled.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，齊獻武王大破尒朱天光等四胡於韓陵，前廢帝鎮軍將軍賀拔勝、徐州刺史杜德於陳降。

translations.literal: day renxu: Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan greatly defeated Erzhu Tianguang and the other four Hu at Hanling; Deposed Emperor Qianfei’s Pacification-General Heba Sheng and Regional Inspector of Xu Province Du De surrendered at Chen.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan shattered Erzhu Tianguang and the four Hu allies at Hanling; Heba Sheng, pacification-general to Deposed Emperor Qianfei, and Du De, inspector of Xu, surrendered at Chen.

sentences.zh: 尒朱兆走趣并州，仲遠奔東郡，天光、度律將赴洛陽。

translations.literal: Erzhu Zhao fled toward Bing Province; Zhongyuan ran to Dong Commandery; Tianguang and Dulu were about to go to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao fled toward Bing; Zhongyuan ran to Dong commandery; Tianguang and Dulu turned for Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 大都督斛斯椿、賈顯智倍道先還。

translations.literal: Grand Commander Husi Chun and Jia Xianzhi returned first by double march.
translations.idiomatic: Grand commander Husi Chun and Jia Xianzhi raced ahead by forced march.

sentences.zh: 夏四月甲子朔，椿等據河橋，懼罪自劾，尋擒天光、度律於河橋。

translations.literal: summer, fourth month, day jiazi, new moon: Chun and others seized the He Bridge; fearing guilt they impeached themselves, then soon captured Tianguang and Dulu at the He Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day, the new moon of the fourth month of summer, Chun’s party seized the He Bridge; though they impeached themselves for fear of blame, they soon took Tianguang and Dulu on the bridge.

sentences.zh: 西北大行臺長孫稚、都督賈顯智等率騎入京師，執尒朱世隆、彥伯，斬於都街，囚送天光、度律於齊獻武王。

translations.literal: Northwest-route Grand Mobile Office Changsun Zhi, Commander Jia Xianzhi, and others led horse into the capital, seized Erzhu Shilong and Yanbo, beheaded them in the capital street, and sent Tianguang and Dulu imprisoned to Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Zhi of the northwest grand mobile office and Jia Xianzhi and other commanders rode into Luoyang, seized Shilong and Yanbo, beheaded them in the market, and sent Tianguang and Dulu in bonds to Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan.

sentences.zh: 辛未，前廢帝驃騎大將軍、行濟州事侯景據城降，仍除儀同三司、兼尚書僕射、南道大行臺、濟州刺史。

translations.literal: day xinwei: Deposed Emperor Qianfei’s Pacification-General Hou Jing held the city and surrendered; he was then made Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, Concurrent Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Southern-Route Grand Mobile Office, and Regional Inspector of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei day Hou Jing, pacification-general to Deposed Emperor Qianfei, surrendered the city and was made equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, concurrent vice director of the Masters of Writing, southern-route grand mobile office, and inspector of Ji.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，以車騎將軍、尚書右僕射魏蘭根為驃騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: day jiaxu: Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wei Langen was made Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu day Wei Langen, grand general of chariots and cavalry and right vice director of the Masters of Writing, was made grand general of agile cavalry and equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，以車騎大將軍、儀同三司、中軍大都督高盛兼尚書僕射、北道行臺，隨機處分。

translations.literal: day yihai: Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, Central-Army Grand Commander Gao Sheng was made Concurrent Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Northern-Route Grand Mobile Office, with discretionary authority.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day Gao Sheng, grand general of chariots and cavalry, equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, and central-army grand commander, was made concurrent vice director of the Masters of Writing and northern-route grand mobile office with full discretion.

sentences.zh: 尒朱仲遠奔蕭衍。

translations.literal: Erzhu Zhongyuan fled to Xiao Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhongyuan fled to Xiao Yan.

sentences.zh: 青州刺史尒朱弼為其部下馮紹隆所殺，傳首京師。

translations.literal: Regional Inspector of Qing Province Erzhu Bi was killed by his subordinate Feng Shaolong; his head was sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Bi, regional inspector of Qing, was killed by his officer Feng Shaolong; his head was sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 丙子，前廢帝安東將軍辛永、右將軍建州大都督張悅舉城降。

translations.literal: day bingzi: Deposed Emperor Qianfei’s Pacification-General of the East Xin Yong and Right General and Grand Commander of Jian Province Zhang Yue held their cities and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day Xin Yong, pacification-general of the east to Deposed Emperor Qianfei, and Zhang Yue, right general and grand commander of Jian, surrendered their cities.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，車駕至河陽，遜位於別邸。

translations.literal: day xinsi: the imperial carriage reached Heyang and yielded the throne at a separate residence.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day the court reached Heyang and the emperor abdicated at a side lodge.

sentences.zh: 太昌元年五月，封安定郡王，邑一萬戶。

translations.literal: fifth month of the first year of Taichang: he was enfeoffed Prince of Anding Commandery, fief ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Taichang year one he was enfeoffed prince of Anding with ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 後以罪殂於門下外省，時年二十。

translations.literal: Later, because of a crime, he died in the outer office of the Gate Department; he was twenty years old.
translations.idiomatic: Later, condemned for crime, he died in the outer quarters of the Gate Department, aged twenty.

sentences.zh: 永熙二年葬於鄴西南野馬岡。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi he was buried at Wild Horse Mound southwest of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi year two he was buried at Wild Horse Mound southwest of Ye.

sentences.zh: 出帝，諱脩，字孝則，廣平武穆王懷之第三子也，母李氏。

translations.literal: Emperor Chu bore the taboo name Xiu, styled Xiaze; he was the third son of Prince of Guangping Wu and Mu Huai; his mother was Lady Li.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Chu bore the taboo name Xiu, styled Xiaze. He was the third son of Prince of Guangping Wu and Mu, Huai; his mother was Lady Li.

sentences.zh: 性沉厚少言，好武事。

translations.literal: By nature he was deep and grave, spoke little, and loved martial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was grave and sparing of speech, and loved the arts of war.

sentences.zh: 始封汝陽縣開國公，拜通直散騎侍郎，轉中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He was first enfeoffed Duke of Ruyang Commandery with an open state and appointed direct-palace scattered cavalier attendant; he was transferred to vice director of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: First enfeoffed state-founding duke of Ruyang, he was made direct-palace scattered cavalier attendant, then vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 建義初，除散騎常侍，尋遷平東將軍、兼太常卿，又為鎮東將軍、宗正卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi he was made scattered cavalier attendant; soon he was transferred to pacifier of the east and concurrent minister of supreme rejoicings; again he was made pacifier of the east and director of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianyi he became scattered cavalier attendant, then pacifier of the east and concurrent minister of supreme rejoicings, then pacifier of the east and director of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 永安三年，封平陽王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongan he was enfeoffed Prince of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongan he was made prince of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，轉侍中、鎮東將軍、[5]儀同三司、兼尚書右僕射，又加侍中、尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Putai he was transferred to attendant, pacifier of the east, [5] equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, and concurrent right vice director of the Masters of Writing; he was again given attendant and left vice director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Putai he became attendant, pacifier of the east, [5] equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, and concurrent right vice director of the Masters of Writing; soon he added attendant and left vice director.

sentences.zh: 中興二年夏四月，安定王自以疏遠，未允四海之心，請遜大位。

translations.literal: summer, fourth month of the second year of Zhongxing: the Prince of Anding, because he was remote in kinship, did not satisfy the heart of the realm; he asked to yield the great throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer in Zhongxing year two the prince of Anding, knowing himself too remote in blood to hold the realm’s loyalty, offered to abdicate.

sentences.zh: 齊獻武王與百僚會議，僉謂高祖不可無後，乃共奉王。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan met with the hundred officials in council; all said the High Ancestor could not be without posterity; together they upheld the prince.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan convened the ministers; all said the dynasty could not lack Gaozu’s line—and together they pressed Xiu forward.

sentences.zh: 戊子，即帝位於東郭之外，入自東陽、雲龍門，御太極前殿，羣臣朝賀。

translations.literal: day wuzi: he took the throne outside the eastern suburb, entered by the Dongyang and Yunlong gates, presided at the Hall of Supreme Ultimate in the front palace, and the hundred officials paid court congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi day he took the throne outside the eastern suburb, entered through the Dongyang and Yunlong gates, sat in the front hall of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, and received the court’s homage.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，昇閶闔門，詔曰：「否泰相沿，廢興互有，玄天無所隱，精靈弗能諭。

translations.literal: When the rites were done he ascended the Changhe Gate and issued an edict: "Decline and peace follow in turn; abolition and establishment each have their season; the dark heaven hides nothing, spirits cannot instruct."
translations.idiomatic: The rites finished, he mounted the Changhe Gate and proclaimed: "Fortune and ruin take turns; thrones fall and rise by season; heaven keeps no secret, and spirits cannot warn what men refuse to see."

sentences.zh: 大魏統乾，德漸區宇，牢籠九服，旁礴三光。

translations.literal: Great Wei inherits Heaven’s stem; virtue spreads through the realm, enfolding the nine domains, reaching beside the three luminaries.
translations.idiomatic: Great Wei holds heaven’s mandate; its virtue fills the realm, gathering the nine domains and shining beside sun, moon, and stars.

sentences.zh: 而上天降禍，運踵多難，禮樂崩淪，憲章漂沒。

translations.literal: Yet heaven sent down calamity; fortune trod through many hardships; ritual and music collapsed, statutes and models were drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Yet heaven sent calamity; hardship followed hardship; ritual and music broke apart, law and pattern sank in flood.

sentences.zh: 赫赫宗周，翦為戎寇；

translations.literal: Majestic was the Zhou house—cut down by barbarian raiders;
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou house stood in glory—then barbarian raiders hewed it down;

sentences.zh: 肅肅清廟，將成茂草。

translations.literal: solemn the clear temple—about to become rank grass.
translations.idiomatic: the clear temple stood in awe—soon to be only wild grass.

sentences.zh: 胡羯乘機，肆其昏虐，殺君害王，刳剔海內。

translations.literal: Hu and Jie seized the moment and unleashed their blind cruelty, killing rulers and princes, flaying the realm inside and out.
translations.idiomatic: Hu and Jie seized their hour and poured out blind cruelty—killing emperors and kings, flaying the realm within and without.

sentences.zh: 競其吞噬之意，不識醉飽之心。

translations.literal: They vied in the will to devour and did not know the heart of drunken repletion.
translations.idiomatic: They competed to swallow all and never knew when greed was sated.

sentences.zh: 自書契以來，未有若斯者已！

translations.literal: Since the age of writing began, there has never been the like!
translations.idiomatic: Since records began, nothing like it has been seen!

sentences.zh: 大丞相勃海王忠存本朝，精貫白日，爰舉義旗，志雪國耻。

translations.literal: Grand Chancellor Prince of Bohai was loyal to the root of the dynasty, his essence piercing the white sun; he raised the banner of righteousness to wash away the nation’s shame.
translations.idiomatic: The grand chancellor, prince of Bohai, stayed loyal to the dynasty’s root, his resolve bright as noon; he raised the righteous banner to wash away national shame.

sentences.zh: 故廣阿之軍，貔虎奪氣；

translations.literal: Thus at Guang’a the army—tiger and leopard seized their breath;
translations.idiomatic: At Guang’a his host struck—foes bold as tiger and leopard lost their breath;

sentences.zh: 鄴下之師，金湯失險。

translations.literal: at Ye the host—metal walls and moats lost their strength.
translations.idiomatic: at Ye the walls of metal and moat failed.

sentences.zh: 近者四胡相率，實繁有徒，驅天下之兵，盡華戎之銳。

translations.literal: Lately the four Hu came in concert—a host indeed numerous; they drove the realm’s armies and mustered all Hua and Rong’s keen blades.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the four Hu marched together—a multitude indeed; they drove the empire’s armies and sharpened every blade of Chinese and barbarian.

sentences.zh: 桴鼓暫交，一朝盪滅，元兇授首，大憝斯擒。

translations.literal: Drums and bells had barely crossed when in one morning all was swept away; the chief culprit yielded his head, the great enemy was seized.
translations.idiomatic: Drums had scarcely sounded when one morning swept them away; the chief culprit lost his head, the great foe was bound.

sentences.zh: 揚旆濟河、掃清伊洛，士民安堵，不失舊章。

translations.literal: Banners were raised to cross the river and sweep Yi and Luo clean; gentry and people rested secure, the old order unlost.
translations.idiomatic: Standards crossed the river and cleared Yi and Luo; people settled in peace, the old order intact.

sentences.zh: 社稷危而復安，洪基毀而還構。

translations.literal: The altars were in peril yet became safe again; the great foundation was broken yet built anew.
translations.idiomatic: Altars tottered yet stood; the great foundation broke yet rose again.

sentences.zh: 朕以託體宸極，猥當樂推，祗握寶圖，承茲大業。

translations.literal: We, entrusted with the imperial body, unworthily meet the age’s push; we reverently grasp the precious chart and inherit this great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: We, set on the imperial frame, unworthily receive the age’s push; we hold the sacred chart and take up this great work.

sentences.zh: 得以眇身，託於王公之上，若涉淵水，罔識攸津。

translations.literal: To place our slight person above kings and dukes is like crossing deep water without knowing the ford.
translations.idiomatic: To set our slight self above kings and dukes is to wade deep water with no ford in sight.

sentences.zh: 思與兆民同茲嘉慶，可大赦天下。

translations.literal: We think to share this blessed celebration with the hundred millions; a general amnesty may be declared throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: We mean to share this blessing with the millions; let there be a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 改中興二年為太昌元年。

translations.literal: The second year of Zhongxing is changed to the first year of Taichang."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxing year two becomes Taichang year one."

sentences.zh: 」詔前御史中尉樊子鵠起復本官，兼尚書左僕射、東南道大行臺，都督儀同三司、徐州刺史杜德討元樹。

translations.literal: An edict restored former Censor-in-Chief Fan Zihu to his original post, made him concurrent left vice director of the Masters of Writing and southeastern-route grand mobile office, and ordered Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies and Regional Inspector of Xu Province Du De to attack Yuan Shu.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored Fan Zihu, former censor-in-chief, to office, made him concurrent left vice director and southeastern-route grand mobile office, and ordered Du De, equal in honor to the Three Excellencies and inspector of Xu, against Yuan Shu.

sentences.zh: 齊獻武王上言，建義之家枉為尒朱氏籍沒者，悉皆蠲免。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan submitted a memorial: households of the righteous army wrongly confiscated by the Erzhu clan were all to be wholly remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan memorialized that families of righteous-army men wrongly seized by the Erzhu should be fully restored.

sentences.zh: 帝以世易，復除齊獻武王為大丞相、天柱大將軍、太師，世襲定州刺史，增封九萬，并前十五萬戶。

translations.literal: Because the age had changed, the emperor again made Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan grand chancellor, pillar of heaven grand general, and grand preceptor; he was to inherit the post of regional inspector of Ding Province; fief was increased by ninety thousand, together with the former making one hundred fifty thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: With the throne renewed, the emperor again made Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan grand chancellor, pillar of heaven grand general, and grand preceptor, hereditary inspector of Ding; his fief grew by ninety thousand households to one hundred fifty thousand in all.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，加齊文襄王侍中、開府儀同，餘如故。

translations.literal: day gengyin: Prince of Qi Wenxiang was given attendant and commissioner with full powers; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin day Prince of Qi Wenxiang received attendant and commissioner with full powers; other posts stood unchanged.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，齊獻武王還鄴，車駕餞別於乾脯山。

translations.literal: day renchen: Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan returned to Ye; the imperial carriage saw him off in farewell at Mount Ganfu.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen day Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan returned to Ye; the court took leave at Mount Ganfu.

sentences.zh: 五月丙申，前廢帝廣陵王殂。

translations.literal: fifth month, day bingshen: Deposed Emperor Qianfei, Prince of Guangling, died.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen day in the fifth month Deposed Emperor Qianfei, prince of Guangling, died.

sentences.zh: 以太傅、淮陽王欣為太師，封沛郡王；

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Prince of Huaiyang Xin was made Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed Prince of Pei Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Xin, grand tutor and prince of Huaiyang, was made grand preceptor and enfeoffed prince of Pei;

sentences.zh: 司徒公、趙郡王諶為太保；

translations.literal: Minister of Works Prince of Zhao Commandery Chen was made Grand Guardian;
translations.idiomatic: Chen, minister of works and prince of Zhao, was made grand guardian;

sentences.zh: 侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、清河王亶儀同三師；

translations.literal: Attendant, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Commissioner with Full Powers Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, Prince of Qinghe Dan—Equal in Honor to the Three Preceptors;
translations.idiomatic: Dan, prince of Qinghe, attendant, grand general of agile cavalry, and commissioner with full powers equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, was made equal in honor to the three preceptors;

sentences.zh: [6]使持節、侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、司州牧、南陽王寶炬為太尉公；

translations.literal: [6] Bearer of the Staff, Attendant, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Commissioner with Full Powers Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, Governor of Si Province, Prince of Nanyang Baoju was made Grand Preceptor;
translations.idiomatic: [6] Baoju, prince of Nanyang, bearer of the staff, attendant, grand general of agile cavalry, commissioner with full powers equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, and governor of Si, was made grand preceptor;

sentences.zh: 侍中、太保、錄尚書事長孫稚為太傅；

translations.literal: Attendant, Grand Guardian, Recorder of Secretariat Affairs Changsun Zhi was made Grand Tutor;
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Zhi, attendant, grand guardian, and recorder of secretariat affairs, was made grand tutor;

sentences.zh: 侍中、驃騎大將軍、尚書左僕射元羅儀同三司、尚書令；

translations.literal: Attendant, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Luo—Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies and Director of the Masters of Writing;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Luo, attendant, grand general of agile cavalry, and left vice director of the Masters of Writing, was made equal in honor to the Three Excellencies and director of the Masters of Writing;

sentences.zh: 驃騎大將軍、吏部尚書元世儁儀同三司。

translations.literal: Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Minister of Personnel Yuan Shijun—Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shijun, grand general of agile cavalry and minister of personnel, was made equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，以齊獻武王固讓，聽解天柱大將軍，減封五萬戶，餘悉如故。

translations.literal: day wuxu: because Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan firmly declined, he was permitted to resign the pillar of heaven grand general post; fief was reduced by fifty thousand households; the rest all remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu day, because Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan declined firmly, he was allowed to lay down pillar of heaven grand general; his fief was cut by fifty thousand households; all else stood.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，以前司空高乾邕復為司空公。

translations.literal: day xinchou: former Minister of Works Gao Gan’ou was again made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou day former minister of works Gao Gan’ou was restored as minister of works.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，帝幸華林都亭，宴羣臣，班賚有差。

translations.literal: On yisi day the emperor visited the Hualin metropolitan pavilion, feasted the ministers, and bestowed gifts in graded measure.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day the emperor visited the Hualin metropolitan pavilion, feasted his ministers, and distributed rewards in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 羽林隊主唐猛突入稱慶，帝以猛犯禁衞，杖之。

translations.literal: Tang Meng, captain of the Feathered Forest guard, burst in proclaiming congratulations; the emperor, because Meng had violated the forbidden guard, had him beaten with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Meng, captain of the Feathered Forest guard, rushed in to offer congratulations; the emperor had him beaten with the staff for breaching the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 猛辭色有忤，斬之階下。

translations.literal: Meng's bearing and words were defiant; he was beheaded below the steps.
translations.idiomatic: Meng answered with a defiant look and tone and was beheaded on the steps below.

sentences.zh: 丁未，詔曰：「無侮惸獨，事炳前經；

translations.literal: On dingwei day an edict said: "Do not wrong the solitary and weak—this principle shines in the classics of old;
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day an edict said, "Do not wrong the solitary and weak—this principle shines in the classics of old;

sentences.zh: 惠此鰥寡，聲留往冊。

translations.literal: show kindness to widowers and widows—its fame rests in past records.
translations.idiomatic: show kindness to widowers and widows—its fame rests in the records of old."

sentences.zh: 朕以薄德，作民父母，乃眷元元，寤言增歎。

translations.literal: We, of slight virtue, serve as father and mother to the people, yet upon the masses Our heart turns and wakes to sighing anew.
translations.idiomatic: We, of slight virtue, stand as father and mother to the people, yet when We turn to the masses Our heart wakes to sighing anew.

sentences.zh: 今理運惟新，哀矜伊始，如有孤老、疾病、無所依歸者，有司明加隱括，依格賑贍。

translations.literal: Now the age's fortune is newly ordered and compassion has but begun: wherever there are the orphaned and aged, the sick, or those with none to rely upon, the officials shall clearly search them out and provide relief according to statute."
translations.idiomatic: Now the age's fortune is newly ordered and compassion has only begun: wherever there are the orphaned and aged, the sick, or those with none to rely upon, the offices shall search them out clearly and provide relief according to statute."

sentences.zh: 」又詔曰：「理有一準，則民無覬覦；

translations.literal: Another edict said: "When principle has a single standard, the people will not look covetously on one another;
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said, "When principle has a single standard, the people will not look covetously on one another;

sentences.zh: 法啟二門，則吏多威福。

translations.literal: when law opens two doors, officials will multiply authority and favor.
translations.idiomatic: when law opens two doors, officials will multiply in authority and favor.

sentences.zh: 前主為律，後主為令，歷世永久，實用滋章。

translations.literal: Earlier rulers made statutes, later rulers made ordinances; age after age it endured, and in practice it grew ever more copious.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier rulers made statutes and later rulers made ordinances; generation after generation it endured, and in practice it grew ever more copious.

sentences.zh: 非所以準的庶品，隄防萬物。

translations.literal: This is not how to set the measure for all ranks and dike in the ten thousand things.
translations.idiomatic: That is not how to set a standard for every rank or fence in the myriad creatures.

sentences.zh: 可令執事之官四品以上，集於都省，取諸條格，議定一途，其不可施用者，當局停記。
