translations.idiomatic: Moqi Pubo was governor of Qin province, attested repeatedly in Zhoushu juan 1 (Annals of Emperor Wen, part 2), Yongxi year 3

sentences.zh: 〈五三四〉
二月、同書卷二文帝紀下大統二年

translations.literal: second month; same book, juan 2, Annals of Emperor Wen, part 2, Datong year 2
translations.idiomatic: second month; Zhoushu juan 2 (same annals, part 2), Datong year 2

sentences.zh: 〈五三六〉
五月、北史卷六齊紀上天平三年

translations.literal: fifth month; Beishi juan 6, Qi annals, part 1, Tianping year 3
translations.idiomatic: fifth month; Beishi juan 6 (Qi annals, part 1), Tianping year 3

sentences.zh: 〈五三六〉
二月、北齊書卷二七万俟普撥傳補。

translations.literal: second month; Beiqishu juan 27, Biography of Moqi Pubo, supplement.
translations.idiomatic: second month; and Beiqishu juan 27 (Biography of Moqi Pubo, supplement).

sentences.zh: 當時有兩秦州，一治上邽，此州自永安三年

translations.literal: At the time there were two Qin provinces, one administered at Shanggui; this province from Yongan year 3
translations.idiomatic: Two Qin provinces existed then. One, with its seat at Shanggui, from Yongan year 3

sentences.zh: 〈五三０〉
變亂軍被鎮壓後，侯莫陳悅、趙貴、李弼、念賢等相繼為刺史

translations.literal: after the rebel army was suppressed, Hou Mochen Yue, Zhao Gui, Li Bi, Nian Xian, and others successively were governors
translations.idiomatic: after the rebel army was crushed, had Hou Mochen Yue, Zhao Gui, Li Bi, Nian Xian, and others as governors in turn

sentences.zh: 〈見周書卷一四、卷一五諸人傳。〉

translations.literal: (see Zhoushu juan 14 and juan 15, biographies of the various persons).
translations.idiomatic: (see Zhoushu juan 14 and juan 15, their biographies).

sentences.zh: 又一是魏末置於汧城的東秦州。

translations.literal: The other was Eastern Qin province, established at the end of Wei at Qian city.
translations.idiomatic: The other was Eastern Qin, set up late in Wei at Qian city.

sentences.zh: 本書卷九肅宗紀孝昌三年記東秦州刺史潘義淵以汧城降變亂軍。

translations.literal: This book, juan 9, Annals of Emperor Suzong, Xiaochang year 3, records Eastern Qin Governor Pan Yiyuan surrendered the rebel army with Qian city.
translations.idiomatic: Juan 9 here (Annals of Emperor Suzong, Xiaochang year 3) records Eastern Qin governor Pan Yiyuan surrendering Qian city to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 太平寰宇記卷三二隴州條歷記沿革。

translations.literal: Taiping huanyu ji, juan 32, Long prefecture entry, lists successive changes.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping huanyu ji, juan 32 (Long prefecture), traces the administrative shifts.

sentences.zh: 万俟普撥當是東秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Moqi Pubo must have been governor of Eastern Qin province.
translations.idiomatic: Moqi Pubo must have governed Eastern Qin.

sentences.zh: 北史卷六齊本紀、北齊書卷二七万俟普撥傳都說高歡平夏州後，万俟普撥率眾投奔東魏。

translations.literal: Beishi juan 6, Qi basic annals, and Beiqishu juan 27, Biography of Moqi Pubo, both say after Gao Huan pacified Xia province, Moqi Pubo led his host to submit to Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Beishi juan 6 (Qi basic annals) and Beiqishu juan 27 (Moqi Pubo) both say that after Gao Huan pacified Xia province, Moqi Pubo led his forces into Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 此「秦州」與夏州相近。

translations.literal: This "Qin province" is near Xia province.
translations.idiomatic: That Qin lay close to Xia province.

sentences.zh: 泰州近在河東，情事不合。

translations.literal: Tai province is near Hedong; the circumstances do not fit.
translations.idiomatic: Tai province stood near Hedong and does not suit the narrative.

sentences.zh: 這裏「泰」乃「秦」之訛，今改正。

translations.literal: Here "Tai" is corruption of "Qin"; now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Tai here is a corruption of Qin; emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 進爵郡王 北史卷五「王」作「公」。

translations.literal: Advanced enfeoffment to prince of a commandery: Beishi juan 5 writes "prince" as "duke."

sentences.zh: 太原王昶特為車騎大將軍 按本書記升遷從無「特為」的寫法，「特」字疑涉下「越肱特」而衍。

translations.literal: Prince of Taiyuan Chang specially made rapid-as-lightning cavalry general. Comment: This book records promotions never with the wording "specially made"; the character "specially" likely was carried down from below "Yue Gong te" and is superfluous.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chang, prince of Taiyuan, was specially made rapid-as-lightning cavalry general. This book never uses "specially made" in promotion formulas; "specially" probably drifted down from the phrase "Yue Gong te" below and should be deleted.

sentences.zh: 己酉椿黨毛鴻賓守潼關齊獻武王破擒之 按北史卷六齊本紀上，高歡攻下潼關在八月，還至洛陽在九月庚寅，周書卷一文帝紀上、北史卷九周本紀上也說高歡襲陷潼關在八月。

translations.literal: Day jiyou: Mao Hongbin of the Chun faction held Tong Pass; the Duke of Qi, Filial and Martial King, broke and captured him. Comment: Beishi juan 6, Qi basic annals, part 1, has Gao Huan take Tong Pass in the eighth month and return to Luoyang on gengyin in the ninth month; Zhoushu juan 1, Annals of Emperor Wen, part 1, and Beishi juan 9, Zhou basic annals, part 1, also say Gao Huan raided and took Tong Pass in the eighth month.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Mao Hongbin of Chun's faction held Tong Pass until the Duke of Qi, Filial and Martial King, stormed it and captured him. Beishi juan 6 (Qi basic annals, part 1) puts Gao Huan's capture of Tong Pass in the eighth month and his return to Luoyang on ninth-month gengyin; Zhoushu juan 1 (Annals of Emperor Wen, part 1) and Beishi juan 9 (Zhou basic annals, part 1) likewise date his seizure of the pass to the eighth month.

sentences.zh: 又據北史魏紀五又說九月己酉是元脩反攻潼關，又克華州之日。

translations.literal: Also according to Beishi, Wei annals, part 5, again says ninth month jiyou was the day Yuan Xiu counter-attacked Tong Pass and again took Hua province.
translations.idiomatic: Beishi, Wei annals part 5, moreover makes ninth-month jiyou the day Yuan Xiu counterattacked Tong Pass and retook Hua province.

sentences.zh: 疑這裏記月日皆有誤。

translations.literal: Suspect here the recorded month and day all have errors.
translations.idiomatic: The month and day given here are probably both wrong.

translations.literal: Comment: Juan 19, part 2, Biography of Prince of Anding Xiu, appendix Yuan Guiping biography, says at Emperor Chu's time "went out as governor of Qing province," and was harmed by Hou Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Juan 19, part 2 (Prince of Anding Xiu, appendix on Yuan Guiping) says that under Emperor Chu he "went out as governor of Qing province" and was killed by Hou Yuan.

sentences.zh: 卷八０侯淵傳敍此事甚詳。

translations.literal: Juan 80, Biography of Hou Yuan, narrates this matter in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: Juan 80 (Biography of Hou Yuan) tells the episode at length.

sentences.zh: 貴平乃青州刺史，侯淵攻取的也是青州。

translations.literal: Guiping was governor of Qing province; what Hou Yuan attacked was also Qing province.
translations.idiomatic: Guiping governed Qing province, and Hou Yuan's target was Qing province.

sentences.zh: 據卷一０六地形志中，青州治東陽。

translations.literal: According to juan 106, Monograph on Geography, part 2, Qing province's seat was Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Juan 106 (Monograph on Geography, part 2) places the seat of Qing province at Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 這裏本作「克東陽」，「陽」訛「楊」或「揚」，後人又妄增「州」字，今改正。

translations.literal: Here the original text read "took Dongyang"; "yang" was corrupted to "Yang" or to the homophone "yang" meaning "to raise," later men groundlessly added the character "province"; now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The original line read "took Dongyang"; yang was miscopied as Yang or as the homophone for "to raise," and later copyists wrongly inserted "province"; all three errors are corrected here.
